channel.title: The Crisp Counter — Kitchen notes & buying guides
channel.description: What to compare before you buy. Question-shaped kitchen buying guides with every figure sourced.

item.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what to compare
item.description: Basket-style or oven-style? Compare the right things: footprint, food shape, capacity zones, cleanup. With the listed values for each format, sourced.

item.title: A no-hype checklist for air-fryer capacity
item.description: Quarts, litres and basket counts don't compare themselves. A five-minute checklist for comparing air-fryer capacity honestly, with listed values.

item.title: Cleanup and counter-space trade-offs, assessed
item.description: What listed dimensions, materials and dishwasher-safe parts say about cleanup and counter space — and how to weigh the trade-off before buying.

item.title: Questions to ask before buying multi-function gear
item.description: Air fry, bake, dehydrate, rotisserie: which functions will you actually use? The questions that separate a worktop workhorse from a cupboard-filler.

item.title: How accurate does a meat thermometer need to be?
item.description: ±0.5°F vs ±1°F, instant-read vs leave-in wireless: what accuracy claims on the listing mean and which thermometer fits which cook.

item.title: How many quarts do you actually need?
item.description: Quarts on a listing describe volume, not people. A serving-count sanity check built from the listed capacities of the three air fryers, each sourced.

item.title: Two baskets or one: when two drawers earn it
item.description: Dual-zone or one big basket? The batch math and the listed specs that decide it: sync finish, shake reminders, and who cooks two dishes at once.

item.title: Holiday hosting: which format earns the counter?
item.description: Big meals, borrowed counter space, eat-in waves. Which air-fryer format and which thermometer workflow fit holiday hosting, from listed specs only.

item.title: Instant-read vs leave-in: which one fits you
item.description: Spot-check in a second, or watch a long cook from your phone? How an instant-read and a wireless leave-in thermometer differ by workflow, with listed specs.

item.title: Gift guide: which of the five fits which cook?
item.description: Match each of the five machines to the cook who would actually use it: weeknight juggling, from-scratch roasting, small kitchens, grill-side checks, long smokes.

item.title: Dual-basket or single-basket air fryer: which?
item.description: Two 3 qt baskets or one 8 qt basket? What the listed capacity, depth and shake-reminder features actually decide, with every figure read from the listings.

item.title: Can you leave a meat thermometer in an air fryer?
item.description: Probe heat ratings, basket depth and what leave-in monitoring means in a small cavity — read from the two listings and the air fryers here, with the gaps left blank.

item.title: Preheat, shake, or don't: rituals, checked
item.description: Preheat or don't? Shake or leave it? What the listed features of these three air fryers actually prompt you to do — and which rituals no listing answers.

item.title: How do you know the turkey is done?
item.description: USDA says poultry is done at 165°F (74°C). How a one-second instant-read and a wireless leave-in probe each answer the question on the big day, from listed specs.

item.title: Buying guide: format, capacity and counter fit
item.description: A buying guide that starts from your kitchen, not a brand: format first, then capacity, then counter depth, then cleanup — with the questions that decide each.

item.title: Where to put the probe: placement beats precision
item.description: USDA guidance on where a thermometer probe actually belongs, set against the two thermometers we follow. What the official pages say, and what they do not.

item.title: Did the air fryer work? One number decides
item.description: Capacity, drawers and wattage do not tell you whether dinner is safe. USDA and extension guidance on the one number that does, applied to the three air fryers we track.
